newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Q3 reports seen boosted by domestic up-tick.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Q3 reports seen boosted by domestic up-tick.

text.p: In the run-up to third quarter earnings reports, equity analysts said they were beginning to favor frequently traded stocks issued by companies focusing on a newly recovering domestic market.

"We feel the best reports will be those posted by firms that concentrate on the domestic market. We expect the economy to turn around and grow by above four percent," said Daniel Romo, equity analyst at the Bancrecer brokerage.
The analysts said they did not expect figures to be spectacular, but they would nonetheless be favorable when compared to a slack third quarter last year.
"Substantial growth may be posted in operating terms, especially when compared to the third quarter 1995, when the domestic market was weak," the Finamex brokerage said.
Companies were not expected to repeat last year's sharp fluctuations in non-cash items after severe adjustments in foreign exchange and interest rates in the quarter ending in September 1995.
The average primary rate for bellwether 28-day Cetes for the first nine months of 1996 was 27.26, compared to year-ago figures of 36.15 percent.

"Lower financial costs and forex losses entered will be very important. Monetary earnings (which include non-cash earnings calculated from outstanding debts revaluated when interest rates rise) will be low," said Roberto Galvan, analyst at the Bursametrica consultancy.
Companies that benefitted from a weak peso last year, mainly exporters, will not be so favored this time round.
"The exchange rate has stood still and companies whose strategies are export-based will not post substantial growth," Romo said.

Analysts said that earnings would depend very much on the particular sector that each company traded in, although the overall outlook was more encouraging in view of the improvement in the overall macroeconomic picture.
"In general, improvements will be very selective on a sectoral basis. Sales and operating earnings will improve as we can see signs of recovery in the domestic market," said Galvan.

Companies in the paper sector, for example, such Kimberly-Clark de Mexico would be favored by a recent reverse in international pulp prices during the third quarter and an upturn in the industry, which should boost earnings in quarter-on-quarter terms.
However, in year-on-year terms, they may be down, because pulp prices, which have roller-coasted this year, were even lower in Q3 1995.
The retail sector, meanwhile, was still lagging behind the economy in general, so analysts expected reports to depend on the performance of individual companies.

"The slump in domestic (consumer) demand will affect results, but efforts have been made to restructure debts and boost sales by special offers, as is the case with Comerci and Gigante. Autrey and Bevides also have favourable outlooks," said Galvan.

Several analysts pointed to construction company Geo, which promotes social housing, and which they expected to benefit from growth in domestic demand and public spending. ICA, another construction firm, was also seen strong.
Analysts said that more favourable prospects for reports could take the Mexican Stock Exchange's blue chip IPC index up to all-time highs at 3,500 points.
"The bourse has plenty of upside potential. At the ners are not stepping in to boost volume, but they will do when reports are posted and the peso softens," said Galvan.
